text:
incident-bot: HIGH: realtime-p95/p99 anomaly detected for hosted inference in us-west-2 — p95 > 1.2s, p99 > 3.5s, error-rate bump 1.2% -> 4.8%. Paging on-call. :pager:

maria: I'm on-call for infra, joining. pulling up traces and SLO dashboard now.

dave: runtime team looking. saw similar blips ~2:10am UTC earlier but resolved. hope not related.

anjali: incoming customer-impact feed shows a handful of active streaming sessions in prod that got stalls. Support flagged 6 sessions with timeouts.

maria: quick sanity checks — rolling median CPU and GPU memory look normal, but queue depth spiking on frontend proxies to 1200 -> 5k. linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/slo/us-west-2/realtime

james: support: which customers? high-risk ones?

support-bot: Customer list: corp-acme, travelly, edu-partner. corp-acme has two active long-running sessions.

elaine: PM note — corp-acme is in pilot with strict latency SLAs, we need to mitigate quickly and notify.

maria: first mitigation — enable conservative routing fallback to a lower-capacity model variant for non-streaming requests to relieve pressure. doing it now: 
```bash
redwood route set-policy --region us-west-2 --policy fallback-small-quant
```

maria: confirmed fallback claim started at 1767770123. routing shift ~10% -> 35% traffic to small-quant.

anjali: I'm checking streaming infra. Observing many long tail opens on connection handshake -> KV cache misses. p99 latency per-chunk spikes to 5s when cache miss rate > 28%. Looks like a cache-eviction storm.

james: can we throttle new streaming sessions for non-enterprise customers while we stabilize?

dave: quick throttle command ready. will apply rate-limits for anonymous and free-tier keys only.

maria: applying per-key token bucket: 
```json
{"action":"apply","scope":"free-tier","max_concurrency":50,"burst":100}
```

maria: throttle applied at 1767770300. observing initial drop in queue depth ~ 20%.

anjali: kicking off a rolling restart for runtime pods that manage KV caches — one-at-a-time to avoid cold start surge. command: 
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serve-runtime -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=serve-runtime-usw2 --grace-period=60
```

anjali: restart step 1/6 started. will monitor.

support-bot: Notifying corp-acme workspace with a brief statement: "We detected transient latency affecting some streaming sessions in us-west-2; mitigation in progress; updates in ~15m."

elaine: nice. include a follow-up offer for a short call if they want immediate remediation.

maria: quick observability checks: flamegraphs for the p99 traces point to heavy scheduling delays in the serving runtime threadpool during prefix cache rebuilds. suspected regression introduced in last-week release (runtime v3.4.1).

dave: I see the v3.4.1 change that moves cache eviction to a GC thread. possible contention with I/O. reverting that patch on a canary node to validate.

maria: canary revert done at 1767770500 — p95 on the canary node dropped from 1.3s -> 270ms, p99 fell ~ 1.1s. promising.

anjali: continuing restarts to rotate nodes onto reverted build. restart 4/6 done. overall p95 is trending down: 1.2s -> 420ms.

maria: live numbers now: p95 420ms, p99 980ms, error-rate back to 1.4%. queue depth stabilized ~900. Not fully resolved but much improved.

james: support — standby to escalate corp-acme if any open sessions need manual migration.

support-bot: corp-acme updated, offered migration. no immediate requests.

elaine: note for incident timeline — initial spike detected at 1767770000, mitigation steps: fallback routing at 1767770123, throttling at 1767770300, canary revert at 1767770500. partial recover by 1767770700.

maria: RCA hypothesis: runtime v3.4.1 cache eviction change increases contention during KV cache rebuild, causing scheduled stalls and tail latency under bursty traffic. Revert validated on canary; rolling revert across us-west-2 in progress.

anjali: post-incident tasks: 1) Full rollback of cache change in prod or safe rework, 2) add circuit-breaker for eviction storms, 3) add per-customer streaming session throttles by default, 4) retro on playbook gaps (cache-warm on restart).

dave: I'll open the PR to revert and include tests that simulate eviction storms (load harness). tagging runtime reviewers.

maria: oncall handoff — I'm handing to anjali for the night. anjali, you'll be primary for follow-up until 1767790000. I'll be reachable.

anjali: ack. monitoring for 2h. if p99 > 1.2s again, page SRE escalation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place, customer notifications sent, rolling revert ongoing. next update 1767771200 or on significant change. :white_check_mark:
